decisions.reason: A classic lever handle line close to the core range has low carrying cost and benefits from long architectural specification cycles, so it is likely to remain in the catalogue.
A multi-model handle family supports the firm's system breadth across budget levels and is unlikely to be withdrawn only four years after launch.
A single design carries somewhat higher rationalisation risk, as the earlier withdrawal of Product D showed, but it still fits the core offer and is likely to stay.
This handle family with several models adds design breadth and is cheap to maintain within the established range.
The flagship electronic access system is central to the firm's digital building organisation strategy and is more likely to be extended or updated than dropped.
